title: exakit
tagline: The one command that runs your local Exasol stack.
role: exakit is the control panel for the Exasol Personal Local Starter Kit: a local Exasol database, the exapump data/SQL CLI, a read-only MCP server your AI client talks to, and the pyexasol Python driver. Everything the kit installs is started, inspected, updated and removed through this one command.

quickstart.note: Deploys the database, loads sample data, and connects your AI clients. Safe to re-run; it resumes.
Status: running means the database is up. Exit 0 running, 3 stopped, 4 not installed.
DSN, users, where the credentials live.
Writes MCP config for Claude, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Continue. Restart the client afterwards.
Bundled sample datasets, or your own CSV / Parquet / JSON file.
Walks through AI clients, SQL clients (DBeaver/DbVisualizer) and Python.

commands.summary: Is the database up and healthy?
commands.description: Shows what is installed, whether each component is healthy, which datasets are loaded, and whether add-on services are running.

commands.summary: What is installed, and what is newer.
commands.description: Kit source and install date, then one row per component and add-on: what is installed, and whether the maintainers advertise something newer. Applying what is waiting is `exakit update`.

commands.summary: Your connection details.
commands.description: The connection panel: DSN, admin and MCP users, where each password file lives, TLS mode and paths. --json prints the install record (manifest.json) verbatim on stdout with nothing else on it.

commands.summary: Friendly walkthrough of every way to connect.
commands.description: How to connect AI clients over MCP, SQL clients (DBeaver or DbVisualizer), and Python via pyexasol.

commands.summary: Start the database and every add-on service.
commands.description: Starts everything the kit runs, deploying the database first if it has never been deployed.

commands.summary: Stop the add-on services and the database.
commands.description: Your data is kept. Bring it back with exakit start.

commands.summary: Come back automatically after a restart?
commands.description: Whether the database and add-on services restart at login: launchd on macOS, systemd --user on Linux, the container restart policy for Nano, a Startup entry on Windows. No argument shows the current state.

commands.summary: Run one SQL statement, with the error translated.
commands.description: Runs a single statement and turns the three faults everyone hits first into their remedy (connection refused -> exakit start; FETCH FIRST/TOP -> LIMIT; object not found -> describe it). Reads only unless --write.
commands.warning: This connects with the starter-kit profile, which is the ADMIN user and is NOT sandboxed. The read-only boundary is the MCP user, not this command.

commands.summary: Load sample data or your own file.
commands.description: Opens the data-loading menu: bundled datasets (tpch, energy, weather) or a local CSV / Parquet / JSON file. Every file kind asks the same two things - the file, then SCHEMA.TABLE - and JSON is shredded into tables by an engine the kit installs for you. --force reloads instead of skipping what is already there.
environment: EXAKIT_DATASETS=tpch,energy,weather names exactly which bundled datasets to load
EXAKIT_SCHEMA sets the default target schema

commands.summary: Every log the kit can show.
commands.description: The installer run, the database container, each add-on service, and what the boot entries wrote at login. No target lists them all with size and last-updated; -f follows one live; --path prints just the path for piping.

commands.summary: Connect your AI assistants.
commands.description: Permanently configures the exasol MCP server in every supported AI client. Existing configs are backed up first. Restart the client afterwards and look for a server named exasol.
environment: EXAKIT_MCP_CLIENTS=claude,codex names clients by name (never menu numbers)

commands.summary: Test and repair the AI connection.
commands.description: Checks the configured MCP clients, repairs what has drifted, then re-checks. Confirms the database is running first. --json reports the diagnosis without repairing.

commands.summary: Show managed MCP state per client.
commands.description: Which clients the kit manages, which config file each one uses, and the current snapshot id.

commands.summary: Validate MCP configs and test connectivity.
commands.description: Checks the managed config files parse and the server answers over stdio.

commands.summary: Remove the managed MCP config.
commands.description: Takes the kit's MCP entry back out of the selected clients. Anything you configured yourself is left alone.

commands.summary: Restore a previous MCP config snapshot.
commands.description: Puts back the latest, or a chosen, backup of the client config files.

commands.summary: List the AI skills the kit carries.
commands.description: One skill per component and add-on, with a one-line summary and whether each has reached the agents' discovery folders.

commands.summary: Install the AI skills for CLI agents.
commands.description: Installs the kit's skills into ~/.claude/skills and ~/.agents/skills so agent sessions can drive the kit. Restart or reload the agent afterwards.

commands.summary: Optional add-ons (dashboards and more).
commands.description: Browse and install optional tools: Space selects, Enter installs. Installed add-ons then update through exakit update. A tool you installed yourself is recognised and never re-offered.
environment: EXAKIT_MARKETPLACE_ADDONS=dash-server answers the menu non-interactively (ids csv, all, or none)

commands.summary: Apply the updates that are waiting.
commands.description: Applies the quick components (kit scripts, exapump, MCP server, pyexasol, installed add-ons) in seconds. A database change stops the database, so it is only applied for an answer the run was actually given: on a terminal you are asked, and an unattended run defers it with the exact command. Your data is kept either way.
environment: EXAKIT_CONFIRM_RUNTIME_UPDATE=1 pre-answers yes to the runtime change
EXAKIT_<COMPONENT>_VERSION pins one component by hand

commands.summary: Rebuild a database that cannot start.
commands.description: For a deployment the launcher reports interrupted where every start fails the same way.
commands.warning: DESTRUCTIVE: the deployment is replaced and its data is not recoverable. Bundled datasets are reloaded afterwards.

commands.summary: Remove what the kit installed.
commands.description: Pick what to remove (Skip, each add-on, or EVERYTHING) with a confirmation summary and a typed gate, or name a single component (exakit uninstall mcp_configs). --dry-run previews the full plan and changes nothing.
commands.warning: A full uninstall removes the database AND its data, the MCP configs, the skills and the binaries.

commands.summary: This screen.
commands.description: exakit help shows the everyday commands. --all lists every command. exakit help <component> (or exakit <component> --help) opens the full reference for one component.

commands.summary: Browse or search every command.
commands.description: Every exakit, exapump and exasol command in one searchable screen. --json prints the whole command surface as one machine-readable object.

environment.name: EXAKIT_MCP_CLIENTS
environment.effect: Which MCP clients to configure, by name: claude, claude_desktop, claude_code, codex, cursor, vscode_copilot, gemini_cli, opencode, continue, all, skip.

environment.name: EXAKIT_DATASETS
environment.effect: Which bundled datasets to load: tpch, energy, weather.

environment.name: EXAKIT_LOAD_SAMPLE
environment.effect: 0 skips data loading, 1 loads the bundled sample.

environment.name: EXAKIT_MARKETPLACE_ADDONS
environment.effect: Answers the marketplace offer: ids csv, all, or none.

environment.name: EXAKIT_REUSE_DB
environment.effect: macOS: 1 adopts an existing database (default), 0 destroys it and deploys fresh.

environment.name: EXAKIT_DB_PORT
environment.effect: Alternate database port (Linux and Windows container path only).

environment.name: EXAKIT_VERSION_POLICY
environment.effect: manifest (default), latest, or pinned - where component versions come from.

environment.name: EXAKIT_CONFIRM_RUNTIME_UPDATE
environment.effect: 1 pre-answers yes to stopping the database for a runtime update.

environment.name: EXAKIT_NO_UPDATE_NOTICE
environment.effect: 1 never prints the once-a-day update notice.

environment.name: EXAKIT_HELP_URL
environment.effect: Where the help documents are fetched from (must be https).

environment.name: EXAKIT_HELP_TTL
environment.effect: Seconds before a cached help document is refreshed. 0 fetches every time.

environment.name: EXAKIT_HELP_OFFLINE
environment.effect: 1 never fetches; renders the copy that shipped with the kit.

troubleshooting.symptom: Docker is installed but not running
troubleshooting.remedy: Start Docker Desktop or run: podman machine start - then re-run the installer.
Stop the other app, or re-run with EXAKIT_DB_PORT=8564 (Linux and Windows).
Re-run the same install command. It resumes from the failed step.
exakit status, then exakit mcp-doctor, then restart the AI client.

troubleshooting.symptom: Another setup run is already in progress
troubleshooting.remedy: Wait for it. If the pid is dead, remove ~/.exasol-starter-kit/.install.lock and re-run.
exakit logs has the full story. Every error message names its remedy.
